chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Few rehearsals in Basie's band, drinking and being fired
summary: In his time the Basie band rehearsed once or twice a week; he drank, dozed under the stage lights, got few solos in the crowded stage shows and was fired.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Just before we get away from the rehearsal thing... .It always surprised me a little when Lester said that about the Basie band, because it seems to sound like such a loose
band, I didn't figure they'd spend a lot of time rehearsing and running through things. But maybe there was a change around this time...

Well, there was. Because when I was in the band, we didn't do all that much rehearsing. You know? We didn't do all that much rehearsing. We rehearsed maybe once or twice a week. You understand? It was a different brand of music than what they later got. And probably that's when Prez left the band, you know... I left the band before Prez did. I mean, I was fired, that is.

Because I was... Well, I'd be talking about... I'll just say I used to get high with juice, you know -- too much juice, I guess. And then I'd go to sleep. Because the light would be shining right in my eyes, and it would shine across the (?) right into my eyes on the stage...
Were you doing a lot of stage shows then?

Yeah. And that beam would get right into my eye. And I'd have to close them, because I couldn't hardly see the music on account of this bright light in my eye. And so, then I didn't have no solo to play, so...you know, there I was. Usually in them stage shows that we had to play, they featured Prez and Buddy and Jo and Buck and Dickie and...
...Sweets... And they had so many soloists in the band, you know. Earle. So...
Seems like Jack Washington never got much to play, and he was such a good baritone player.
No, he didn't either. And there was...oh, what's his name that played the other trombone...?
Dan Minor. He never got a chance to play anything either.
I think he recorded one solo with the band.

Yeah! So you know, like, we didn't have too much to do. So... He didn't drink like what I did, you know, because I guess he had his wife looking after him to keep him from...keep him from...you know, keep him from drinking so much. Ah, that's the way I was.
